extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media innovators, news organizations, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational 'About' page describing the Nieman Journalism Lab's mission, goals, projects, licensing, and fellowship information for those interested in journalism's future and reuse of Lab content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight attempts at innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab aims to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab will surface experiments and new approaches in journalism to study their outcomes and derive lessons; this is a central editorial priority rather than a strict scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find good ideas for others to steal
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to find good ideas for others to steal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab prioritizes identifying practical, re-usable ideas and approaches that other journalists or organizations can adopt; emphasis on actionable takeaways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help reporters and editors adjust to online work
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and coverage should support practitioners in adapting skills, workflows, and mindsets for online journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help traditional news organizations survive
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to help traditional news organizations find a way to survive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab focuses on coverage and analysis that can inform strategy and decision-making for legacy news organizations facing digital disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help startups that will complement or supplant traditional news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: We want to help the new crop of startups that will complement — or supplant — them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage includes new ventures and startup models in the media ecosystem, with an eye toward what makes them viable or influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a collaborative exchange of ideas with readers' contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among [our smart people] are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab solicits and values reader participation and contributions as part of its editorial process; community input is an explicit part of how the site operates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial stance: be fundamentally optimistic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab adopts an optimistic approach to the future of journalism — that viewpoint informs tone and selection of stories (looking for solutions and opportunities rather than purely pessimistic accounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default copyright resides with Harvard (or the original author); exceptions will be noted where applicable. Users should check attribution notices for individual pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content licensing: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License
rubrics_metrics.description: Also unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (a) you are not using it for commercial purposes; (b) you attribute it to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the work’s author, preferably with a link back to the original content; and (c) you release any work you build on top of our work under a similar license. Examples given: translating the site into Portuguese, redistributing posts to students, using the Twitter feed as lyrics — all allowed under these conditions. For any other use, contact the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Foundation mission: promote and elevate standards of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Help advance the Nieman Foundation’s mission 'to promote and elevate the standards of journalism'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab is a project of the Nieman Foundation and aligns with its broader mission; content and initiatives should contribute to critical examination and improvement of journalistic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project encourages reporters and editors to monitor and hold accountable those who exert power in all aspects of public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lab supports and highlights watchdog reporting as a journalistic value — investigative scrutiny and accountability are emphasized as important practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowships: program description and application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual deadline to apply for a fellowship is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, procedural information for prospective fellows: the Foundation administers the oldest fellowship program for journalists and accepts applications on the stated annual schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Reports purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Nieman Reports, the nation’s oldest magazine devoted to a critical examination of the practice of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation publishes Nieman Reports to analyze and critique journalistic practices; the Lab’s coverage is positioned alongside these institutional resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encyclo: chronicling key players in journalism’s evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Encyclo is our encyclopedia of the future of news, chronicling the key players in journalism’s evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encyclo is presented as a project/resource that catalogs organizations and actors important to media innovation; inclusion implies significance to the field's development.
